episodes.168187: Afternoon thunderstorms produced gusty outflow winds.
episodes.168453: An extensive line of strong to severe thunderstorms swept across the western Nebraska Panhandle during the mid afternoon hours on 5/29, producing isolated pockets of damaging wind gusts in excess of 60 MPH. A peak wind gust of 70 MPH was observed at the Scottsbluff RAWS site. High wind gusts also resulted in tree damage at Lake Minatare, where an injury occurred when a male teenager was hit in the chest with a falling tree branch. The victim was taken to the hospital and was reported to be in good condition.
episodes.168455: A line of strong thunderstorms developed along the Laramie Range during the early afternoon hours on the 29th, before advancing quickly eastward toward the Nebraska state line. These storms generally produced wind gusts around 50 to 55 MPH. A peak wind gust to 61 MPH was observed at the Torrington Airport.
episodes.168530: A line of severe thunderstorms tracked northeast from northeastern Wyoming and expanded east-northeast across northwestern South Dakota. Wind gusts to 65 mph were recorded across portions of the area.
episodes.168531: A thunderstorm became severe as it tracked east-northeast across Bennett and Todd Counties. Hail around quarter size and eventually wind gusts around 70 mph accompanied the storm before it weakened over eastern Todd County.
episodes.168559: One storm that  moved through western Orange County become severe and produced hail.
episodes.168677: A surge of deep tropical moisture from the northwest Caribbean Sea as high pressure built across the western north Atlantic resulted in numerous showers and scattered thunderstorms.  Several areas of gale-force wind gusts developed from thunderstorm outflows.
episodes.168686: Thunderstorms moved up the James River Valley during the late evening and early morning hours of May 28th and May 29th respectively. Storms occasionally produced wind damage as they moved into the Prairie Coteau region, with a peak wind speed of 74 mph in Lake City.
episodes.168687: Strong to severe thunderstorms impacted a large portion of the Sandhills and north central Nebraska during the evening, overnight into the morning hours of May 29-30th. Thunderstorms initiated over the northwestern Sandhills and tracked east across the area. The thunderstorms were in association with an approaching cold front and strong upper level disturbance. Hail up to six inches in diameter and thunderstorm wind gusts up to 60 MPH were reported with the strongest storms.
episodes.169838: An upper level disturbance moved across the region, spreading showers and thunderstorms across the region. While widespread severe weather was not observed, a few high based storms did produce strong outflow winds.
episodes.170165: Several upper low pressure systems moving across northeast OR in late May produced several rounds of heavy rain in the Blue Mountains and along the foothill locations. Several reports of water over local roadways, washouts of gravel roads, and heavy rain were reported during the day on May 29th.
episodes.170216: Thunderstorms developed toward midnight on leading elevated warm advection across south central South Dakota and progressed rapidly northeast through areas north of Interstate 90.  Large amounts of DCAPE in the air mass resulted in spotty damaging wind.  A second cluster of storms developed on the tail end of the initial storms on the nose of an increasing low-level jet, using up to 2000 J/kg of elevated instability to rapidly become severe.  Very large hail resulted as storms first developed supercellular characteristics, and then a mix of hail and damaging wind as short bowing segments evolved moving into northwest Iowa and southwest Minnesota.

episodes.170369: A mid/upper level low pressure area over the eastern Gulf of Mexico helped to draw high moisture levels across South Florida. Light winds and the formation of sea breezes helped to focus numerous showers and thunderstorms over the near shore waters and Lake Okeechobee.
episodes.170373: A mid/upper level low pressure area over the eastern Gulf of Mexico helped to draw high moisture levels across South Florida. Light winds and the formation of sea breezes helped to focus numerous showers and thunderstorms over the interior and eastern parts of South Florida, causing gusty thunderstorm winds, hail, and flooding over parts of the area.
episodes.170473: Scattered severe thunderstorms brought damaging winds and large hail to the area during the morning, with a second round of severe storms during the mid-afternoon.
